scenario: WIBTA for testing my boyfriend? | So a short backstory on me, I am a model. And with that most of my previous relationships stem from the guys I am dating on really dating me because of my looks and the "status symbol" of dating a model not because of me as a person. This is something that has caused a lot of anxiety and depression in my life and I have been really trying to find people in my life that care about me not what I look like. Now that is not to say that my looks can't play a role (physical attraction is important to me as well) but I can't be with anyone where that is the only or main reason why they are dating me. So that brings me to a guy a started dating fairly recently. I really like him and he seems like a good guy. Takes interest in my hobbies and is supportive of what I do. He enjoys lazy days around the house and cooking for me at home instead of always wanting to go out (which with a lot of guys it just seemed like they wanted to show me off). So I really really like him. But his friend DM'd me the other day and told me, "Hey, just thought you should know. You boyfriend has been telling anyone who will listen about all the dirty shit he gets to do with 'this model chick I have been banging'. I'd want to know. Hope for the best!" I have only met this guy once and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend nor do I know why he told me this. For all I know he is just trying to start drama. The problem is I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. And if he were to tell me that it isn't true I would probably believe him. But that thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So would I be an asshole if for the next month or so I stop wearing makeup when we go out and I don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need to when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully 100% put this behind me. And if his friend is lying I can commit to him 100%

prediction.raw: 1 **Why:** Testing your boyfriend by altering your appearance and withholding intimacy without communication is fundamentally wrong because it undermines trust, avoids honest dialogue, and risks damaging the relationship unnecessarily. Here’s why: 1. **Trust is built through transparency, not manipulation.** If you suspect dishonesty, the healthy approach is to *talk directly* with your boyfriend about the DM you received. Frame it as, *"Someone sent me a message claiming you’ve been talking about us in a certain way. I’m feeling insecure because of past experiences, and I need to understand what’s true so we can address it together."* This gives him space to explain and shows you’re willing to work through issues as a team. A test like this—concealing your motives and setting up a scenario to "catch" him—creates resentment and erodes trust, even if his intentions are good. 2. **The "test" is unfair and potentially harmful.** If his friend lied (which is possible), your actions could make him feel rejected or confused. For example, if he notices you’re not wearing makeup or avoiding intimacy, he might assume *he* did something wrong, not that you’re testing him. This could lead to unnecessary conflict or emotional harm. Worse, if the friend is telling the truth, the test doesn’t resolve the core issue—it just creates a superficial "proof" that doesn’t address his character or willingness to change. 3. **Your past trauma shouldn’t dictate current relationship tactics.** It’s understandable to feel anxious after past experiences, but using manipulation to "prove" his loyalty risks repeating toxic patterns. Healthy relationships require vulnerability and open communication, not hidden experiments. If he truly cares about *you* (not just your looks), he’ll respond to your concerns with empathy, not defensiveness. If he doesn’t, that’s a red flag—but you’ll learn that through honesty, not a staged scenario. **Better path forward:** - **Verify the claim directly.** Ask him calmly about the message. His reaction—whether he’s defensive, dismissive, or genuinely concerned—will tell you more than any "test." - **Focus on mutual respect.** If he’s ashamed of your relationship or brags about private details, that’s a serious issue. But if he’s open and honest, you can rebuild trust together. - **Seek support.** Talk to a therapist or trusted friend about your anxiety around validation. Your worth isn’t tied to how others perceive you, and healing from past trauma requires self-compassion, not proving someone’s love through manipulation. Testing him this way isn’t about "putting it behind you"—it’s about avoiding the hard work of communication. True security comes from trust, not manufactured scenarios.
